title: Back Squat
summary: A barbell back squat for the quads, glutes and adductors, and the main lower-body strength lift.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: barbell (Olympic bar); weight plates; rack with J-hooks (power rack, squat stands or bench uprights).

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for quads (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly quads total.
Library rating 0.7 for glutes (helper): each working set adds 0.7 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.6 for adductors (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly adductors total.
Library rating 0.4 for lower back (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly lower back total.
Library rating 0.25 for abductors (minor): each working set adds 0.25 of a set to the weekly abductors total.
Library rating 0.15 for abs: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly abs total.

setup.text: Set the bar on your upper back, step out and stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and your toes slightly out.
Brace your core and sit down between your hips, with your knees tracking over your toes.
Go as deep as you can while keeping your back neutral, ideally with your hip crease below your knee.
Drive back up through your mid-foot.

form_cues.cue: Sit down between your hips with knees tracking toes
Drive up through the whole foot
Depth matters. Deep squats build more quad and glute than half reps.

mistakes.text: Letting the knees cave in on the way up.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds two or three ramp-up sets at rising loads before the first working set, unless that load is very light.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 6-10 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Set safety arms or pins where you can fail a rep safely, or use a spotter, and use collars.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.
